paper: Seeing Before Reasoning: A Unified Framework for Generalizable and Explainable Fake Image Detection
verified_identity: Kaiqing Lin, Zhiyuan Yan, Ruoxin Chen, Junyan Ye, Ke-Yue Zhang, Yue Zhou, Peng Jin, Bin Li, Taiping Yao, and Shouhong Ding. arXiv:2509.25502v1, submitted 2025-09-29; official OpenReview indexed camera-ready PDF is labeled ‘Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026’. The arXiv record lists only v1. The OpenReview final PDF link was identified, but its page returned a browser-verification challenge and that file was not independently read.
relevance_class: Direct, high-relevance AI-generated-image-forensics explanation-quality evaluation; not a local image-editing/splicing attribution experiment
scope_and_methods: Targeted review of the official arXiv v1 HTML: problem framing, method/data construction, explainability results, conclusion, and Appendix E.2–E.3. ExplainFake-Bench randomly samples 400 fake images each from Chameleon (spelled ‘Chemeleon’ in the arXiv HTML) and GenImage++, total 800; instructions are randomly phrased and MLLM explanations are scored by GPT-4o. The judge receives the image, ground-truth label, and explanation, and assigns 1–5 scores for correctness, specificity, logical consistency, factual accuracy, and instruction following. The prompt says an incorrect final judgment should cause each dimension to be heavily penalized (≤2). Forensic-Chat Stage 1+2 reports 4.5363 correctness, 3.9461 specificity, 4.4048 logical consistency, 3.8158 factual accuracy, 4.4236 instruction following, and 4.2253 mean. Prior screening of all 65 reference positions and existing Scholar result identities was reused, not repeated.
observed_reliability_evidence: Direct external scoring of explanation outputs against the visible image and ground-truth label, covering decision correctness, concrete detail, logical coherence, image-content factual consistency, and instruction following; this is more informative than qualitative heatmap display or text-similarity alone. The reported 4.2253/5 mean and per-dimension scores document the benchmark’s measured output quality for this sample and judge protocol.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: ExplainFake-Bench contains 800 fake/generated images and no real-image examples, so it does not establish explanation quality on both classes or balanced real-world authenticity cases. GPT-4o is the sole reported judge; no human-expert calibration, independent second-rater agreement, test-retest/repeated-judge stability, or judge calibration is reported in the reviewed protocol. The judge sees both image and label, which supports image-grounded assessment, but there is no independent artifact-region/claim gold standard; specificity is not localization overlap. Correctness is entangled with every other dimension because a wrong judgment forces all dimensions to ≤2, so composite scores mix detector correctness and explanation quality. Visual plausibility/factual consistency does not test whether cited evidence causally drove the detector’s decision; no deletion/insertion, counterfactual, parameter-randomization, or appropriate-reliance test is reported. Gemini-2.5-Pro generates training captions, commonsense inversions, and dialogues (Appendix E.2); no independent factual audit of those seeds was located in the reviewed sections. The final ICLR PDF was not independently read because OpenReview returned a browser-verification challenge; detailed claims above are tied to official arXiv v1 HTML and the indexed OpenReview publication label. This review does not reopen the prior 65-position bibliography screen or citing network.
screening_conclusion: Retain rank 55 as a strong direct paper for image-forensics explanation quality: its GPT-4o protocol explicitly inspects the image and label and scores five explanation dimensions. Report it as externally judged output-quality/factuality evidence, not validated causal faithfulness or appropriate reliance. Preserve the one-class sampling, single-judge, and correctness-penalty limits; reuse all existing Scholar identities and the earlier 65-reference screen.
